basics.description: Findable deploys into this subscription and resource group. Every resource is created new, with managed identities only: no keys, no connection strings. Every resource is created in the Region unless you give it a region of its own: when this subscription cannot create the Azure AI Foundry account or the Cosmos DB account in the Region, or the Region does not offer the models, the checks below say so and a box under each lets you create that one account in another region while everything else stays in the Region (the search service has the same box on the Size tab). An existing resource group pins the Region to its own; to deploy elsewhere, create a new resource group. Do not change the Region once the Summary page has validated: the portal created the resource group then, in the Region of that moment, and the deployment goes into the group's region; give a resource its own region here instead, or start again in a new tab with a new resource group name.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: The Azure region every Findable resource is created in, unless a resource is given a region of its own (the Foundry account and Cosmos DB below, the search service on the Size tab). Only regions that offer the web app, the Foundry account, the search service, Cosmos DB and Key Vault are listed; the checks below say whether this subscription can create the Foundry account and the Cosmos DB account there and whether the models are offered. An existing resource group pins the Region to its own region: to deploy elsewhere, create a new resource group.

basics.name: baseName
basics.label: Deployment name
basics.subLabel: The seed for every resource name
basics.toolTip: 3 to 17 lowercase letters and digits. Every resource is named after it; the web app, the storage account, the Cosmos DB account, the search service and the AI accounts add a 7-character suffix so the name stays unique across Azure (the web app becomes https://<name>-<suffix>.azurewebsites.net; the deployment's webAppUrl output has the exact address).

constraints.validationMessage: Use 3 to 17 lowercase letters and digits with no other characters.

options.text: Names that must be unique across Azure (the web app, the storage account, the Cosmos DB account, the search service and the Foundry account) get a 7-character suffix computed from the resource group and this name, so any name works and a redeploy into the same resource group keeps the same names. The install needs an Azure AI Foundry account that offers the models and a Cosmos DB account: an error appears below when this subscription cannot create one of them in the Region or the Region lacks a model, with a box to create that one account in another region. The Size tab checks the App Service tier and the search service the same way.

This subscription cannot create an Azure AI Foundry account (kind AIServices, S0) in any region, and Findable needs one, so the deployment would fail whichever Region is chosen. A Free Trial, Azure for Students or a similar offer cannot create Azure OpenAI or Foundry accounts, and Azure may not yet have opened them to a brand-new subscription or tenant (https://aka.ms/locationineligible). Pick another subscription in the Subscription field above (the list refreshes for it), upgrade this one to pay-as-you-go, or ask Microsoft support for Azure AI Foundry access (Help + support, Service and subscription limits (quotas), Cognitive Services) and start this wizard again.

basics.name: cosmosElsewhere

elements.name: searchElsewhere
elements.label: Create the search service in another region
elements.toolTip: Azure AI Search refuses a new service in a region whose search capacity is spent (InsufficientResourcesAvailable: East US 2 on 2026-11-02, Basic and Standard alike) and offers no check before creation. Tick this to create only the search service in a region of your choice; everything else stays where the Basics tab put it. Keyless skillset billing has no same-region requirement.

elements.name: searchRegion
elements.label: Search service region
elements.toolTip: The region of the search service alone, from the regions open to this subscription. The quota check below reads Azure AI Search in this region; whether the region has search capacity left shows only when the deployment creates the service.

options.text: [concat('This subscription has used its quota of ', if(equals(steps('sizing').sizePreset, 'production'), 'Standard', 'Basic'), ' search services in ', if(steps('sizing').searchElsewhere, coalesce(steps('sizing').searchRegion, location()), location()), ', and Findable needs one, so the deployment would fail there. Create the search service in another region (the box above), choose the other preset, or ask for a higher limit (Help + support, Service and subscription limits (quotas), Azure AI Search).')]

[concat('Azure AI Search answered nothing for ', steps('sizing').searchRegion, ': the region may not offer the service, or the quota read failed. The deployment fails there when the region lacks Azure AI Search.')]

No check reads the search capacity Azure has left in a region: a region whose capacity is spent refuses the service only when the deployment creates it, with InsufficientResourcesAvailable (East US 2, 2026-11-02). When a deployment fails that way, deploy again into a new resource group with the search service in another region (the box above), which moves only that service.

elements.name: semanticRanker
elements.label: Semantic ranker on the search service
elements.toolTip: Reranks search results with the semantic ranker (free tier on Trial, standard on Production). Azure offers it in most regions but not all, and there is no way to check before deploying: if the deployment fails creating the search service, switch this off and deploy again.

elements.name: logRetentionDays
elements.label: Log retention (days)
elements.toolTip: How long the Analytics-plan tables keep Findable's logs. Basic-plan tables (Trial) keep 30 days.

options.text: Azure charges for these resources on this subscription, separately from the Findable license. Cosmos DB is serverless and Storage is standard tier in both presets.

elements.name: licenseKey
elements.toolTip: The key from your Findable welcome email (it starts with FNDL1). Leave it empty to enter it on the License page after the first sign-in; the installation does not run until a valid key is entered. Keys and renewals: support@findable.net.

constraints.validationMessage: A Findable license key reads FNDL1.<payload>.<signature>; paste the whole key.

options.text: Every trial is 30 days. The key is verified by the application, never sent to Findable, and can be replaced on the License page at any time.

When the deployment finishes, open the address in the deployment's webAppUrl output (Outputs on the deployment page: https://<deployment name>-<7-character suffix>.azurewebsites.net). The site shows its Connect tenant page with one script to run in Azure Cloud Shell as an administrator of the tenant: the script creates the two app registrations and the administrators group, writes them onto the web app, and the site opens signed in. Nothing else to configure. Role assignments can take up to ten minutes to apply after the deployment reports success. Support: support@findable.net.
